findings.claim: The step that retires an earlier attempt's insights also supersedes scored, merged and shown (client-visible) insights. It leaves no record of why they were retired, so their reasons are lost, and their dependents (Actions, notes) are orphaned.

commit_note: Security has two block rounds. The .md and .json name the HIGH at 8862f85 and again at f367eb4 (the round-two commit). The same finding was raised in both rounds.

findings.claim: retireIfShown (src/pipeline/recompute.ts) marks a hidden original (rejected, unresolved or quarantined) as superseded once its rerun is shown. That makes it match clientInsightSql's standing-in rule (superseded, with nothing later released), so a client can see an insight the strategist rejected while its rerun waits for release. Raised at 8862f85 and again at f367eb4.

findings.claim: In the scoring retry's check-before-render path, a verification that was truncated (did not complete) is treated as passed or checked, so insights are rendered as verified when they were not fully checked.

Under the shared-attribution rule, both are listed here. No files are stated; the paths below are inferred from the commit's file list.

findings.claim: The plan's questions for the person (what only the company can answer) are stored with origin plan_derivation. As a result the Bounty paths ignore them, research spawns them as research questions, and the next config save switches them off.
When a plan is still short of its chosen size after the retry, this is only logged. The plan page still claims the selected size, so the shortfall is hidden from the person.

findings.claim: The insights-writing time history used for estimates counts edits and recomputes along with insights written in a research cycle, so the 'time left' estimate is built from unlike work.

commit_note: The .md table says 'BLOCK at 92d4f28 (two HIGH)' but does not say which items were HIGH. These two are inferred: they are the first two items in the .md's list and the leading items in the title of the next commit (cb020a7). Treat the attribution as an inference.

findings.claim: The notification's action button has no click handler on company pages that do not load the page script, so the action silently does nothing there.
When the read of a run's topics fails, the notice falls back to a false 'Did not start' message, and the failure is neither logged nor said.

commit_note: The .md table says code-reviewer returned 'BLOCK at 481e16b and 79ad551' (two block rounds). The 481e16b finding is listed first and the 79ad551 finding second.

findings.claim: At 481e16b: a failed brand read (site fetch or parse) overwrites the company's stored brand with empty values, wiping the brand that was kept before.
At 79ad551: a failed fetch of a brand asset (logo or font face) wipes the stored brand asset instead of keeping the earlier one.

commit_note: The .md table says security returned 'BLOCK at 79ad551 (unvalidated font CSS; migration)' after passing 481e16b with MEDIUMs. The severity is not stated; the block threshold for this reviewer is CRITICAL. The report gives only the one word 'migration' for the second finding.

findings.claim: Font CSS taken from the client's site is stored and served inline without validation. The font rules are not built from checked fields, and the stored font_css can contain '<', which lets site-supplied content break out of the style context in served pages.
Migration 123 does not correctly carry the brand columns the code relies on, so a database other than the one aligned by hand lacks them.

commit_note: The .md table says code-reviewer returned 'BLOCK at 8b23763 (Deep asks could not act; subject scope)'. That was its only block round. Files are inferred from the commit (src/brain/research-act.ts, src/brain/tools.ts).

findings.claim: When the person asks Ed in Deep mode, the Research operator actions are not available, so Ed cannot carry out what the person asked.
Ed's Research actions are not correctly scoped to the current subject (company), so an action can run with the wrong subject scope.
